title: App colours
summary: The user picks one of the palettes of design/tokens.json appThemes and a chat background. The palette sets the accent colours, the own chat bubble, the chat background and the app icon at once, and the app redraws in the new colours.

palette.description: The palette id, in appThemes order.

background.description: The chat background id, in appThemes.chatBackground.options order.

isSelected.description: true for the stored chat background.

options.description: All palettes, in appThemes order. The default palette (acai) is first.

backgrounds.description: All chat backgrounds, in appThemes.chatBackground.options order. The default (marca) is first.

pick.effect: Keeps the palette on the phone, sets the app theme at once (no restart) and switches the app icon to the icon of the palette. Plays the tick haptic.

pickBackground.effect: Keeps the chat background on the phone and shows it at once in every chat. Plays the tick haptic.

notes: Opens from the row colors in Conversas e mídia (registries/settings.json). The row value is the title of the stored palette.

Each option shows the app icon of the palette (a white mark on BipePalette.iconBackground, the same picture as the home screen icon), its title, and a check on the selected one. The selected state is the check and the accessibility selected trait, not the colour alone.

What follows the theme (bipe-chat/bipe#811, MZ 2026-10-27): the tokens in appThemes.themed (accent.ink, accent.fill, accent.fillPressed, accent.wash, bubble.own), in light, dark and high contrast. Trust colours (trust.verified included) never change. The Bipe logo and wordmark, the launch screen and onboarding stay acai.

Storage: the palette id under bipe.settings.palette, on the phone only. iOS keeps it in the app group defaults, so the share extension reads the same palette. A missing or unknown id is the default palette.

iOS: the icon changes with UIApplication.setAlternateIconName (BipePalette.alternateIconName; nil is the primary icon). iOS shows its own alert after each change; the app cannot hide it. A failed change keeps the theme and leaves the icon as it was.

Android: one launcher activity-alias per palette, all with the same intent filter; the app enables the alias of the palette and disables the others (PackageManager.DONT_KILL_APP). Some launchers move or drop the home screen icon after the change.

Palettes (MZ, 31 October 2026): six fruits with the most colour distance at the same contrast. Goiaba (hue 355) and pitanga (hue 42) keep off danger red (hue 27); caju left the picker because it sits on caution amber. A stored id that is no longer a palette (caju) is the default palette.

Chat background (ADR 0213, MZ 2026-11-01): a second section, titled bipe_chats_background, below the palettes, with its footer. marca (default) draws BipeChatBackground blobs and marks on chat.background; cor is chat.background alone; liso is surface.base, the timeline as before. The chat.* tokens are themed, so every option follows the palette.

The chat background fills the timeline behind the messages and stays still while they scroll. The marks are the app icon shape, upright (BipeMark). Places and sizes come from BipeChatBackground: x and y are fractions of the timeline width and height, a mark side is a fraction of the shorter side and a blob radius a fraction of the longer side.
High contrast: every chat.* token is the flat palette colour, so marca looks like cor. ink.primary on chat.background is AAA in every palette (tools/lib/gen-tokens.mjs).
Storage: the id under bipe.settings.chatBackground, next to the palette (iOS app group defaults, Android settings file). A missing or unknown id is the default (marca).
